name: Village Center (Avenida San Martin)
tagline: The walkable heart of El Chalten
description: The compact core along Avenida San Martin holds most hostels, cafes, restaurants, tour offices, and the craft brewery. Everything sits within a short stroll, trailheads are minutes away, and the seasonal traveller buzz concentrates here. It is the most practical and social base for a trekking-focused stay.
vibe: Lively, sociable, and convenient in season
bestFor: First-time visitors and social trekkers wanting everything on foot
pros: Central to shops, cafes, and tour offices
Best access to services and food
cons: Busiest and priciest area in high season
Can feel crowded on summer evenings

name: Northern Edge (Fitz Roy / Laguna de los Tres Trailhead)
description: The quieter northern fringe of town sits closest to the trail up to Laguna de los Tres and the Fitz Roy viewpoints. Guesthouses and cabins here favour early-rising hikers who want the shortest walk to the trailhead and calmer surroundings away from the main street bustle.
bestFor: Serious trekkers prioritizing the Laguna de los Tres route
pros: Shortest access to the Fitz Roy trailhead
cons: Slightly further from restaurants and shops

name: Southern Edge (Cerro Torre Trail / Bus Terminal)
description: The southern end of the village sits near the Cerro Torre trailhead and the bus terminal, making it convenient for arrivals, departures, and the Laguna Torre hike. Lodging here suits travellers who value easy bus connections to El Calafate alongside quick trail access.
bestFor: Travellers valuing bus access and the Cerro Torre route
pros: Close to the bus terminal for El Calafate
Handy for the Laguna Torre trail
cons: A short walk from the main street cluster
Limited dining right at this edge

name: El Calafate (Nearby Services Base)
description: About three hours away by bus, El Calafate is the region's bigger hub, home to the FTE airport, more reliable services, wider dining and lodging, and the Perito Moreno glacier. Some travellers base here for infrastructure and day-trip or bus into El Chalten for the trekking.
vibe: Bigger, busier, more serviced tourist town
bestFor: Those needing better connectivity, flights, and amenities
pros: Wider range of services and lodging
cons: Three hours from El Chalten's trailheads
